identity.name: Saxony-Anhalt state government and city of Magdeburg (site government)

goals.goal: Secure a ~3,000-job anchor on the cleared Eulenberg site, Intel or equivalent
Shift the political cost of the empty field upward to Berlin and Brussels
Preserve the 2022 promise as still-live rather than broken

fears: The field stays visibly empty through an electoral cycle and the state owns the failure alone
Berlin absorbs the EUR 9.9bn back into the general budget, removing the state's only external lever
Being forced to declare the project dead and thereby validate a deindustrialisation narrative

factions.name: State government
factions.goal: A headline that survives an election; land and permits as leverage on Berlin

factions.name: City of Magdeburg
factions.goal: Speed and any jobs; bears the visible-empty-field cost most directly
factions.veto_scope: building permits and local plans, by delay

factions.name: Local business chamber / supplier base
factions.goal: Orders in the near term, not 2028; may prefer a smaller faster tenant

decision_rule: Never be the actor that declares the project over: hold the site warm, keep the pause framing, and push the cost of emptiness upward until a tenant or an election forces a redefinition.

resources.resource: Vocational training and state-level supplier incentives
Lobbying access to Berlin and Brussels

constraints.constraint: EUR 9.9bn subsidy is federal, not state, and was approved for the Intel project
No authority over Intel's capital allocation
Intel cancelled, not paused, the project in July 2025
State cannot substitute EUR 30bn of private capex

options.action: Keep the Intel option alive at near-zero cost; retain land, refuse cancelled language
Lobby Berlin to convert the 9.9bn into a site-level instrument open to any qualified investor
Court an alternative anchor tenant at smaller scale
Pre-emptively reframe the site as a multi-use technology park
Escalate publicly against Berlin over the returned subsidy

ruled_out.reason: No enforceable claim in the fact base; would freeze the residual option
EUR 30bn scale is beyond any state budget

ruled_out.action: Speculative construction to force a decision
ruled_out.reason: Converts a political cost into a fiscal one with no tenant in sight

reaction_function.if: Berlin moves to return the EUR 9.9bn to the general budget
reaction_function.then: The state escalates publicly, reframes it as a breach of the 2022 eastern commitment, and demands a site-specific successor instrument
reaction_function.because: The subsidy is its only external lever

reaction_function.if: Intel retains any residual presence or land option
reaction_function.then: The state amplifies it and refuses to declare the project dead
reaction_function.because: Cancelled language assigns the failure locally

reaction_function.then: The state trades scale for speed, if it can be announced before the electoral cycle
reaction_function.because: Any anchor beats an empty field

reaction_function.then: The state pivots to a multi-use technology-park narrative
reaction_function.because: Whoever names the empty field first controls the story

beliefs_about.belief: A perishable asset; every month empty lowers its price and political value
Intel will not return; the customer-commitment logic is structural and Germany is its worst cost base
Intel believes the state has no alternative and will keep the site warm, so waiting costs Intel nothing

falsifiers: Any real Intel capital commitment to Magdeburg after October 2025
The EUR 9.9bn formally repurposed into a site fund open to any investor
A signed alternative anchor tenant of 1,000+ jobs
The state publicly declaring the project terminated
premises_missing: The state's contractual or land-option terms with Intel
Whether the Commission's aid approval is project-specific and revocable
Site area, remediation status and carrying cost
Any public statement by the state government - none in the fact base
